title: No incremental compiler session API; interactive clients cannot hold definitions, generations, or JIT bindings
summary: mncs-compiler exposes no session concept: no create/define/commit/publish/abandon API and no session verbs on the mncs CLI. A host REPL loop over batch compilation would fake persistence by rebuilding temporary programs, so Lab ships no live session and specifies the missing policy in MNCS instead (mncs.lab.session, 11 passing tests).
requiredBehavior: A compiler-owned incremental session API: create/drop a session, analyze a fragment against prior state, commit a generation, invalidate dependents, inspect artifacts - as sketched in mncs-lab docs/compiler-boundary.md.

reproducer.text: mncs --help shows batch routes only; mncs-compiler kernel.mncs excludes session inputs. See mncs-lab pressure/reproducers/no-session-api/.

observation.summary: Session capability absent at mncs-language 066897e; policy specified in MNCS without a live session.

reproduction.instructions: List mncs CLI verbs (no session route) and confirm kernel.mncs session exclusion; see reproducer.

evidence.summary: mncs --help offers compile/test/experiment/call/observe; no session verb exists.
mncs-compiler kernel.mncs: session inputs explicitly out of scope.
Session policy (lifecycle, generations, reset matrix) specified in mncs.lab.session with 11 passing native tests.

workaround.description: Policy modeled in MNCS; no host-side fake session. Workaround is the absence of a live REPL, which is intentional.
